battle.name: 凱撒內戰
battle.theater: 盧比孔河至法薩盧斯戰線
battle.brief: 公元前四十九年一月，凱撒率第十三軍團跨過盧比孔河，與元老院主導的龐培聯軍全面開戰，戰場由意大利北部的盧比孔河與馬西利亞，轉到希臘的法薩盧斯，再延伸到西班牙的蒙達。卡面的野驢式投石機是羅馬圍城戰的標準器械，與攻城塔、撞錘配合壓制城頭、掩護進逼。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 這場內戰的兩邊都出自羅馬共和國本身，沒有外國軍隊以征服者身分介入，這是它與其他戰爭最大的不同。凱撒一方是執政官儒略·凱撒領袖的人民黨陣營，骨幹是他在高盫戰爭中一手帶出來的第十三軍團、第十軍團等老兵，以及從山南高盫與北意大利各城邦徵來的補充兵員；凱撒本人握有山南高盫與伊利里亞的總督權與指揮權，這支軍隊實質上只聽命於他個人。對面則是元老院主導的貴族派聯軍，總指揮為龐培：龐培本人在西班牙，戰事初期兵力約二萬八千至三萬，另在敘利亞有西庇歐家族、在高盫有梅里達方向的多支部隊，亞歷山大的托勒密王朝一度以艦隊與糧食支援龐培。意大利境內由多米提烏斯·阿赫諾巴布斯據守馬西利亞，卡爾凱·波西烏斯·加圖以護民官身分在元老院主導抵抗；朱巴二世在父親阿德希巴爾於公元前五十九年去世後被帶到羅馬，在凱撒家中長大，公元前四十五年蒙達之戰時以努米底亞軍隊站在凱撒一邊。東地中海方面，埃及的托勒密十三世先站在龐培一方，公元前四十八年凱撒兵臨亞歷山大後改為凱撒的盟友並提供船舶與糧食；敘利亞、猶太與塞琉古諸地仍由元老派將領控制，等於給凱撒的對手留了一條地中海東岸的後方。
countriesEn: Both sides of this civil war came out of the Roman Republic itself; no foreign army entered as a conqueror, and that is what sets this war apart from most others of its kind. Caesar's side was the populares camp led by the consul Gaius Julius Caesar, its backbone the XIII and X legions he had raised and trained himself during the Gallic wars, together with replacements levied from Cisalpine Gaul and the Italian municipalities. Caesar held the governorship and the command in Cisalpine Gaul and Illyricum, and in practice that army obeyed him and nobody else. Opposite him stood the senatorial optimates coalition under Pompey. Pompey commanded in Spain with a force estimated at some twenty-eight to thirty thousand men, additional columns were held by the Scipios in Syria and by other commanders on the Gallic and Spanish fronts, and the Ptolemaic kingdom of Alexandria supplied Pompey with ships and grain in the opening phase. In Italy, Domitius Ahenobarbus held Massilia, while Cato the Younger, praetor of the plebs, led the resistance inside the senate. Juba II, whose father Adhibal died in 59 BC, was taken to Rome and raised in Caesar's household, and he fought for Caesar with the Numidian contingent at Munda in 45 BC. In the eastern Mediterranean the Ptolemies at first stood with Pompey; after Caesar reached Alexandria in 48 BC they became his allies and supplied him with ships and grain. Syria, Judaea and the Seleucid territories remained in senatorial hands, giving Caesar's opponents a rear base on the far shore of the Mediterranean.
people: 凱撒與龐培是這場戰爭的兩根樁柱。凱撒在布倫迪西翁的海岸面對無船可用的僵局時，靠對元老院的不信任與對自己軍隊的把握作出決斷；跨過盧比孔河後，他在科爾菲尼烏姆接受多米提烏斯·阿赫諾巴布斯的投降，隨後以不等對方集結的速率逼近羅馬，逼得元老院在軍隊逼近城門前出城西遷。龐培則以資深統帥之姿在西班牙整軍，先以艦隊接走凱撒的對手，再於羅馬陷落前退出義大利，轉進希臘與小亞細亞，最後在法薩盧斯被正面擊破，翌年逃往埃及並遇害，終身未能重返意大利。拉比耶努斯原是凱撒在高盫最倚重的副手，公元前四十九年倒戈投向龐培，在西班牙以少量兵力拖住凱撒，又在西庇歐戰役中擔任主戰指揮，公元前四十五年與小龐培一同陣亡於蒙達，馬庫斯·李錫尼烏斯·克拉蘇斯亦死於此役。凱撒陣中，除老兵團的士卒外，馬克·安東尼自公元前五十二年起任財務官隨軍，西塞羅在羅馬以演說與書信替凱撒爭取輿論，德西穆斯·布魯圖斯與馬庫斯·尤尼烏斯·布魯圖斯先後加入，後者更在內戰結束後成為刺殺凱撒的策動者。卡爾凱·波西烏斯·加圖在烏提卡拒降自盡，寧可讓自己的政治生命終結，也不肯把赦免的權柄交到凱撒手上。
peopleEn: Caesar and Pompey are the two pillars of this war. Facing a stalemate on the coast at Brundisium with no fleet to move his army, Caesar chose to act on his distrust of the senate and on his confidence in the loyalty of his own troops; once over the Rubicon he accepted the surrender of Domitius Ahenobarbus at Corfinium and then advanced on Rome at a rate the senate could not match, forcing the senators to leave the city westward before his men reached the walls. Pompey reorganised his army in Spain, picked up Caesar's opponents by sea, and evacuated Italy before Rome fell, carrying the cause into Greece and Asia Minor. He was finally broken in open battle at Pharsalus, fled to Egypt the following year and was killed there, never returning to Italy. Titus Labienus had been Caesar's most trusted lieutenant in Gaul; he defected to Pompey in 49 BC, held Caesar at bay in Spain with a small force, and commanded the Pompeian army in the fighting against Scipio. He was killed at Munda in 45 BC together with the younger Pompey, and Marcus Licinius Crassus also died on that field. On Caesar's side, beyond the veterans of the legions, Marcus Antonius served as military treasurer from 52 BC, Cicero worked in Rome for Caesar's cause with speeches and letters, and Decimus Brutus and Marcus Junius Brutus joined in turn, the latter becoming one of the plotters of his assassination. Cato the Younger refused terms at Utica and killed himself, preferring to end his own political life rather than hand the power of pardon to Caesar.
kits: 卡面這具野驢式投石機是羅馬圍城戰的標準器械，名字得自發射後劇烈回彈、彷彿野驢踢腿的模樣；羅馬人自己多半稱它為擲石機，與發射弩矢的弩砲分開。維特魯維斯在《建築十書》第十卷記載其構造：厚重的木製機身靠四道扭力束拉緊主梁，長臂由底部絞盤的繩索壓出，一發石彈需九人操作，安置石彈、絞緊扭力、上弦擊發與傳令各司其職；主梁承受不住回震時，維修工匠要當場更換部件。它重達數百公斤，只能架在固定陣位上，離開營壘的車載弩砲在卡雷戰役中被帕提亞騎射手全部摧毀，說明這類野砲一旦離開陣地便難以自保。因此在這場內戰裡，投石機的戰術位置很清楚：它不是野戰的決定火力，而是與攻城塔、撞錘、藤棚配合的攻城火力節點。馬西利亞之圍，凱撒造出二十五座攻城塔與十二具撞錘；阿瓦里庫姆之圍，他備有六十尺高攻城塔、五十尺長撞錘，並堆出寬三百三十尺、高八十尺的攻城土壘，作業時以擲石機與弩砲壓制城頭。羅馬軍裝本身相對單純：重標槍、長劍與大盾構成步兵骨架，頭盔、胸甲與釘鞋標準化，騎兵用寬刃彎刀與長矛，凱撒最倚重的是高盫與巴達維亞的騎兵，遠征希臘時更靠從亞歷山大徵得的海運維持。
kitsEn: The wild-ass stone thrower shown on the card was the standard engine of the Roman siege, and it is named for the way the arm kicks back after release as if an ass were lashing out; the Romans themselves usually called it a stone-throwing catapult, keeping it distinct from the bolt-shooting ballista. Vitruvius describes the machine in the tenth book of his treatise on architecture: a heavy timber frame draws a main beam tight with four torsion bundles, the long throwing arm is powered by ropes run off a winch at the base, and a single stone needs a crew of nine, divided among those who set the stone, those who wind the torsion, those who cock and release, and those who signal. When the beam cannot survive the recoil, the engineers replace the part on the spot. The engine weighs several hundred kilograms and can only be sited in a fixed emplacement; the wheeled bolt-throwers that went into the field with the army were all destroyed by Parthian horse archers at Carrhae, which shows that engines of this kind cannot protect themselves once they leave the camp. In this civil war the tactical role of the stone thrower is therefore clear: it is not the deciding firepower in the field, but a node of siege firepower worked in concert with siege towers, battering rams and covered galleries. At the siege of Massilia Caesar built twenty-five siege towers and twelve battering rams; at Avaricum he had a tower sixty feet high, a battering ram fifty feet long, and raised an assault mound three hundred and thirty feet wide and eighty feet high, with stone throwers and bolt-throwers in support to keep the defenders off the wall. The Roman soldier's own equipment was comparatively simple: the heavy javelin, sword and large shield formed the infantry frame, helmets, body armour and nailed sandals were standardised, cavalry used broad curved blades and long spears, and Caesar relied above all on Gallic and Batavian horsemen, sustained overseas by sea transport requisitioned at Alexandria.
tactics: 凱撒的攻城有一套固定程序：先以外圍壕溝與土壘切斷城的外援，再用藤棚與攻城塔在箭雨下平行推進，把撞錘送到牆根，最後以齟甲護住突擊隊或從城下掘地道。阿瓦里庫姆城門前，凱撒一方掘地道反制對方挖出的坑道時，順著坑道挖出對方正在進攻的地下通道，整批殲滅守軍。野戰方面，凱撒沿用三列縱隊：重裝兵在前，輕裝兵在後，第三列留作反騎兵預備隊；法薩盧斯之役他把第三列散開成楔形，專候龐培的騎兵衝擊，龐培卻把騎兵按兵不動，直到右翼突破才齊驅直入，凱撒右翼因此被壓垮，第十軍團自側面轉入才扭轉戰局。狄拉基烏姆的攻防則完全是土木工程：凱撒沿海岸修出約十五英里的連續防線與三十座外圍堡壘，龐培反過來在凱撒營外築起自己的包圍牆，兩道牆之間就是消耗戰。補給線是另一個關鍵，凱撒在意大利與伊利里亞靠每夜宿營、每日定量行軍維持徵發制，在希臘則面臨梯希安平原歉收造成的饑餓，糧船必須從亞歷山大與意大利橫渡地中海，冬季在伊利里亞的泥濘道路上行軍更把隊伍拖散。
tacticsEn: Caesar's sieges followed a fixed procedure: first a trench and an earthen rampart to cut the city off from outside help, then covered galleries and siege towers advanced side by side under arrow fire to bring the battering ram to the foot of the wall, and finally a testudo to cover the assault, or a mine driven under the defences. Before the gates of Avaricum, when Caesar's miners ran into an enemy gallery of their own making, they followed the enemy tunnel and broke into the chamber where the besiegers were working, destroying them in one stroke. In the field Caesar kept the three-line formation: heavy infantry in front, light troops behind, and a third line held back to counter enemy cavalry. At Pharsalus he spread that third line into a wedge to receive the Pompeian charge, but Pompey held his horsemen back until his right had broken through and then sent them in all at once; Caesar's right wing gave way under that weight, and the X legion turned in from the flank to reverse the battle. Dyrrhachium was fought almost entirely as a matter of earthworks: Caesar built a continuous line of roughly fifteen miles along the coast with thirty outer redoubts, and Pompey answered by raising his own circumvallation against Caesar's camp, the two lines of works turning the ground between them into a grinding attritional contest. Supply was the other decisive factor. Caesar kept his army on a requisition footing in Italy and Illyricum through a camp every night and fixed daily marching distance, but in Greece he faced hunger caused by a poor harvest in the Thessalian plain, with grain ships having to cross the Mediterranean from Alexandria and Italy, while winter marching on the mud roads of Illyricum stretched his columns until they fell apart.
data: 可考的數字大致如下，跨來源常有出入，只能當量級看。公元前四十九年凱撒在意大利手中的兵力約一萬五千人，另有高盫與西班牙的分遣隊；他在《內戰記》中自稱全軍約三萬，而元老派在帝國各地合計約九萬步、十五萬騎，這個對手總數出自凱撒自己的宣傳，應打折看待。法薩盧斯之役，凱撒方面的說法是己方步兵約二萬二千、騎兵約三千，龐培陣前步兵約一萬二千、騎兵約七百，龐培的騎兵總數雖佔優，卻敗在戰術保守。狄拉基烏姆的連接防線長約十五英里，凱撒後來在龐培營外築成的包圍牆約六英里、設二十五座堡壘。攻城器械方面，馬西利亞之圍有二十五座攻城塔與十二具撞錘；阿瓦里庫姆的攻城塔高六十尺，約十八公尺，撞錘長五十尺，約十五公尺，土壘寬三百三十尺，約一百公尺，高八十尺，約二十四公尺。野驢式投石機每具約需九人操作，射完一發要重新上弦、絞緊扭力束、校正瞄準，遠不足以像弩砲那樣連發。石彈以石灰岩或大理石製成，另有鉛製投石索彈丸與弩砲鐵鏃。關鍵日期為：公元前四十九年一月十日跨盧比孔河，公元前四十八年六月九日法薩盧斯之役，公元前四十五年三月十七日蒙達之役，公元前四十四年二月凱撒出任終身獨裁官，同年三月十五日遇刺。
dataEn: The recoverable figures are roughly as follows; they vary between sources and should be read as orders of magnitude. In 49 BC Caesar had about fifteen thousand men in Italy, with detachments in Gaul and Spain. In his own Commentaries he claimed a total force of roughly thirty thousand, while he put the senatorial side at about ninety thousand foot and fifteen thousand horse across the empire, a figure that comes from Caesar's own propaganda and has to be discounted. For the battle of Pharsalus, Caesar's version gives his own army as about twenty-two thousand foot and three thousand horse, with Pompey having about twelve thousand foot and seven hundred horse on the field; Pompey had the larger cavalry force but lost through tactical caution. The continuous defensive line at Dyrrhachium ran about fifteen miles, and the circumvallation Caesar later raised against Pompey's camp about six miles with twenty-five redoubts. For siege equipment, the siege of Massilia involved twenty-five siege towers and twelve battering rams; at Avaricum the tower stood sixty feet high, roughly eighteen metres, the ram was fifty feet long, roughly fifteen metres, and the assault mound was three hundred and thirty feet wide, roughly a hundred metres, and eighty feet high, roughly twenty-four metres. A wild-ass stone thrower needed about nine men to work, and after each shot the torsion had to be rewound, the bundles retightened and the aim reset, so it could not fire anything like the rate of a bolt-thrower. Stones were cut from limestone or marble, and there were also lead sling bullets and iron bolts for the bolt-throwers. The key dates are: the crossing of the Rubicon on 10 January 49 BC, the battle of Pharsalus on 9 June 48 BC, the battle of Munda on 17 March 45 BC, Caesar's appointment as dictator for life in February 44 BC, and his assassination on 15 March of the same year.
cause: 直接導火線在公元前四十九年一月初。凱撒在高盫作了十年將軍，握有經過戰爭淬鍊的軍隊、屬於他個人的聲望，以及高盫的戰利品與盟友，這三者讓元老院無法安心。政治上，公元前六十二年至前五十九年間元老院多次企圖削弱凱撒的權力，前五十九年凱撒出任執政官後與龐培同任，一年後取得高盫與伊利里亞的指揮權，此後十年不經選舉連任，這在共和國憲制下是前所未有的。前五十四年凱撒之女茱莉亞去世，婚姻紐帶斷裂，前五十年初在拉維納的會議上凱撒當著元老院使者的面駁斥其撤職要求，雙方敵意再無掩飾。羅馬的制度本來就無法處理一個靠私人軍隊維持權力的執政官：元老院先後用分權、限制與拖延消耗他，公元前五十二年甚至立法禁止執政官離開意大利超過一年、任職滿期後不得以將軍身分指揮戰役，等於逼凱撒要麼放棄軍隊、要麼放棄權位。前四十九年一月七日元老院通過法令，要求凱撒解散軍隊、交出行省，否則以公敵論處；凱撒在魯比亞的軍中讀到消息，決定先開戰，把「骰子已經擲下」這句話留在記錄裡，隨即率第十三軍團越過界線。
causeEn: The immediate spark came in early January of 49 BC. Caesar had been a general in Gaul for ten years, and he held an army hardened by campaign, a reputation that belonged to him personally, and the plunder and allies of Gaul; no one of these three could be tolerated by the senate. Politically the senate had tried repeatedly between 62 and 59 BC to cut Caesar down. He was consul in 59 BC alongside Pompey, and a year later took command in Gaul and Illyricum, then held it for ten years without re-election, something without precedent in the republican constitution. In 54 BC Caesar's daughter Julia died and the marriage bond broke; at a meeting at Ravenna in early 50 BC Caesar openly rejected the senate's demand for his dismissal before its envoys, and after that the hostility between the two men was bare. The Roman constitution was in any case unable to cope with a consul sustained by a private army: the senate answered with divided commands, restrictions and delay, and in 52 BC even legislated that a consul must not leave Italy for more than a year, nor command a province as a general after his term expired, which forced Caesar to give up either his army or his legal position. On 7 January 49 BC the senate passed a decree requiring Caesar to disband his army and surrender his provinces, on pain of being declared an enemy of the state. Reading the news in his camp at Rubbia, Caesar decided to strike first, leaving the words that the die was cast in the record, and led the XIII legion across the line.
impact: 這場內戰在制度層面的後果遠大於戰場勝負。凱撒打贏之後保留了共和國的選舉、議會與法庭，卻讓這些機構失去制衡他的能力；執政官任期變成他的工具，終身獨裁官的名分則把個人的軍權與政治權綁在一起，不須經過元老院同意。元老院在他治下只是一個排場，接著而來的是以戰爭剩餘資源換來的安置：公元前四十九年把公民權給予山南高盫居民，公元前四十六年改革曆法，前四十四年開始在殖民地安置退伍老兵。從此羅馬進入內戰時代，蘇拉與馬略的舊例還在，但每一次內戰都由「救國」的名義開始，最後以軍隊決定誰能執政的模式收場，屋大維終於在公元前十一年以奧古斯都之名把這套模式制度化。凱撒的名字本身成為王權的代名詞，皇帝戴凱撒的冠冕，東歐語言裡「凱撒」就是皇帝；他不只改變了羅馬，也改變了後世一切以軍力奪權的政變想像。
impactEn: The institutional consequences of this civil war far outran its battlefield results. Having won, Caesar kept the elections, the assemblies and the courts of the republic, but he stripped them of any power to check him. The consulship became an instrument of his own, and the title of dictator for life bound personal military command to personal political authority without the need for senatorial consent. The senate under Caesar became a formality, and what followed was a settlement paid for out of the war's surplus: citizenship for the inhabitants of Cisalpine Gaul in 49 BC, the reform of the calendar in 46 BC, and the planting of veteran colonies beginning in 44 BC. Rome entered the age of civil wars; the precedents of Sulla and Marius were still there, but every civil war now began under the slogan of saving the state and ended with the army deciding who would rule, and Augustus finally gave that pattern a permanent form in 27 BC. Caesar's own name became shorthand for monarchy: emperors wore the laurel of Caesar, and in the languages of eastern Europe the word for Caesar is the word for emperor. He changed not only Rome but the later imagination of every coup that seized power at the point of a sword.

resultEn: On 9 June 48 BC at Pharsalus the main body of Pompey's army was broken in open battle; he fled with a handful of followers into Thessaly and was killed on the Egyptian coast the following year. In 46 BC Cato the Younger refused terms at Utica and killed himself. On 17 March 45 BC at Munda Caesar turned a losing battle against odds of roughly twenty thousand to between thirty and fifty thousand, on broken ground of hills and low walls built around trees; the younger Pompey, Labienus and Marcus Licinius Crassus were all killed, and at one point Caesar very nearly lost the field when his line of retreat was closed. Caesar returned to Rome, held the consulship for successive years, and in February 44 BC was made dictator for life, after which the senate voted him a series of extraordinary honours, including the title of father of his country. In form the institutions of the republic continued to work; in substance power in Rome was now concentrated in a single man. The military phase of the civil war ended there, and the political reckoning it had opened was only beginning: on 15 March 44 BC Caesar was killed in the theatre of Pompey, and the second triumvirate inherited at once the armies and the unresolved question of legitimacy left behind by the war.
